title: A Nation of Many Faiths
objective: After this level you can explain how immigration since 1965 widened American religion, and what surveys show about Americans' faith today.
summary: The 1965 Immigration and Nationality Act opened America to new Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist and Sikh communities. In 2023 to 2024 about 62% of US adults were Christian, 29% unaffiliated, 7% other.

cards.headline: In 1965 a law changed who could move to America, and how America prays.
cards.body: Today mosques, temples and gurdwaras stand in nearly every major American city. Here's how that happened, and what Americans say about their faith now.

cards.headline: Opening the door
cards.body: The Immigration and Nationality Act, signed on October 3, 1965, ended America's long policy of limiting immigration by national origin, opening new doors for immigrants from Asia. Muslims, Buddhists, Hindus, Sikhs, Jains and Zoroastrians arrived, along with new communities of Jews and Catholics. Now mosques, temples and gurdwaras stand in virtually every major city.

cards.headline: New faiths, familiar ones too
cards.body: Newcomers didn't only bring new faiths. Christians remained most legal immigrants: 68% in 1992 and 61% in 2012. Over those same years, the share belonging to religious minorities rose from about one in five to one in four.

cards.headline: America today
cards.body: Pew's 2023 to 2024 Religious Landscape Study surveyed 36,908 adults. About 62% identified as Christian, 29% as religiously unaffiliated and 7% with other religions, among them Jews, Muslims, Buddhists and Hindus. After years of decline, the Christian share shows signs of leveling off. And belief runs wider than belonging: 83% said they believe in God or a universal spirit.

mascot.line: Don't memorize the decimals. Six in ten Christian, three in ten unaffiliated, the rest other faiths.

cards.headline: A Nation of Many Faiths: the takeaways
learned: The 1965 immigration law widened America's faiths
Christians stayed the majority of new immigrants
About 62% of US adults were Christian in 2023 to 2024

questions.prompt: What did the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965 end?

options.label: Limits on immigration by national origin
All immigration from Europe
options.rationale: It ended national-origin limits, not European immigration.

questions.explanation: Signed October 3, 1965, the act ended the policy of limiting immigration by national origin.

questions.prompt: Put these groups in order of their share of US adults in Pew's 2023 to 2024 study, largest first.
questions.explanation: About 62% of US adults identified as Christian, 29% as religiously unaffiliated and 7% with other religions.

questions.prompt: Pew found 29% of Americans unaffiliated, yet 83% believe in God or a universal spirit. Using Level 9, how can both be true?

options.label: One of the two figures must simply be a survey error
options.rationale: Both come from the same careful study.

options.label: The unaffiliated are all atheists, so they're counted twice
Affiliation is reported identity; many unaffiliated still believe
The census measured one number, and Pew measured the other
options.rationale: The census doesn't ask about religion.

questions.explanation: Surveys measure the identity people report, and 'none' doesn't mean no belief.
